 The Remarried Empress tops Disney+ local premieres in 3 days and 50+ markets, but no view count 
 Intermission 
 Disney+ K-drama The Remarried Empress tops Korean premieres in 50+ markets
 Most viewed local original premiere ever on Disney+ and Hulu after three days, by Disney's own count, with no view total. What the record measures and omits.
 by Luis Rijo

 The Walt Disney Company said on November 6, 2026 that The Remarried Empress, a Korean romantic fantasy series adapted from a NAVER WEBTOON, had become the most viewed local original premiere of all time on Disney+ and Hulu globally, a ranking built on three days of views after the series launched on November 3. The same announcement said the series ranked as the number one Korean title premiere in over 50 markets, among them the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Spain, Germany, Mexico, Chile, Australia and New Zealand (listed together as ANZ) and Canada.
 What the announcement did not include was a number. There is no view count, no hours figure, no name of the title that held the record before, and no definition of what Disney counts as a local original. For advertisers buying Disney's streaming inventory, the claim is a ranking without a denominator.
 In Short
 Disney says a new Korean drama on Disney+ and Hulu had the biggest three-day start ever for one of its local originals, and was the top Korean premiere in more than 50 countries. That matters because Disney sells ads on these services, and hits made outside the US can draw viewers in many countries at once. But Disney did not say how many people watched, so nobody outside the company can check how big the record really is.
 What Disney claimed
 The announcement, posted in the Entertainment section of Disney's corporate newsroom, makes two separate claims, and they are worth keeping apart. The first is an all-time ranking: The Remarried Empress is "the most viewed local original premiere of all time on Disney+ and Hulu globally, based on 3 days of views following its launch on November 3." The second is a market-by-market ranking: the series "currently ranks as the number one Korean title premiere in over 50 global markets."
 The second claim is narrower than it first appears. It compares The Remarried Empress against other Korean title premieres, not against every premiere in those markets. A number one Korean premiere in the United States is not the same as a number one premiere in the United States. Disney named nine entries in its list of more than 50 markets, and one of those entries, ANZ, covers two countries. The remaining markets were not listed.
 Disney supported the announcement with press reaction rather than data. According to Disney, The Chosun Daily called the series a "global triumph," while Collider described it as "your next must-watch fantasy romance." No Disney executive was quoted.
 The pre-launch numbers
 Three figures in the announcement relate to demand before the series reached the platform. Preview screenings at the Busan International Film Festival sold out, according to Disney, though no screening count or date was given. The payoff trailer drew 13 million views in the first 48 hours after its debut on YouTube and social media platforms. That figure combines several platforms and gives no split between them. The original webtoon has drawn nearly 3 billion views since it was first released, according to Disney, which did not say when that was.
 Each of these is a measure of attention to the property rather than to the series itself. The webtoon figure in particular describes an audience built over years on a different company's platform, NAVER WEBTOON, before Disney's adaptation existed.
 A premiere moved forward by a day
 The series was originally scheduled to premiere on Wednesday, November 4. It instead debuted on Tuesday, November 3, which Disney described as "a special thank you to fans for their overwhelming support." A related Disney newsroom post from November 3 carried the headline that the series premiered a day early on Disney+ and Hulu.
 The timing has an arithmetic consequence. With a November 3 launch, a three-day window closes at the end of November 5, which allowed a ranking to be published on Friday, November 6. Under the original November 4 date, the same three-day window would have run through November 6 itself. The release does not say whether November 3 counts as day one, or whether the window is measured in calendar days or 72-hour periods.
 What the announcement does not say
 Several gaps limit what the record can tell anyone outside Disney.
 There is no absolute number. Disney did not publish total views, hours streamed or the number of accounts that started the series. Without that, the ranking cannot be compared with any other title on any other service.
 There is no definition of a view in the release. When Toy Story 5 reached 20 million views worldwide in its first five days on Disney+ in September 2026, Disney's own post did not define the term either. Earlier Disney disclosures, as reported by trade outlets, treated a view as total stream time divided by the title's runtime. If that method applies here, partial viewing counts as a fraction of a view, and the result depends on the runtime of the episodes available in the window as well as on how many people pressed play.
 There is no definition of "local original." In general industry use, local originals are series or films a streamer commissions for one national market, in that market's language, with local writers, cast and production companies. Disney's announcement does not say whether its comparison set includes every non-US original across Asia Pacific, Europe and Latin America, or only Korean titles, or whether Hulu originals produced outside the US are counted.
 There is no named predecessor. A record implies a previous holder. Disney did not say which title The Remarried Empress passed, or by how much.
 There is no third-party measurement. The ranking is Disney's own count of activity on Disney's own services. No measurement company is named.
 There is no mention of advertising. The release does not say how many of the views came from ad-supported plans, whether the series carries ads in every market where it streams, or what the audience looked like by age or household.
 The release schedule and why it matters
 Four episodes were available at launch. Two new episodes will follow every Wednesday from November 11 through the series finale on November 25, exclusively on Disney+ and Hulu, according to Disney. By PPC Land's count, that is three more Wednesdays and six more episodes, which would bring the series to ten episodes if each remaining drop contains two. Disney did not state the total episode count.
 The weekly cadence sets this series apart from the full-season drops that streaming made familiar. A weekly schedule stretches a title's presence on the service over most of a month, and it is built for appointment viewing , in which audiences plan to watch at release rather than waiting to binge. Research PPC Land covered in 2025 suggests the format can affect attention as well as reach: TVision found that viewers of weekly-release content paid 67% attention in the first week, against 61% for binge viewing of binge-released content , based on its panel of 5,000 US homes in the first half of 2025.
 The finale falls on Wednesday, November 25, the day before Thanksgiving in the United States and two days before Black Friday, so the weekly run overlaps the start of the US holiday shopping period. Disney did not connect the schedule to advertising in its announcement.
 The series and its source
 The Remarried Empress follows Empress Navier and her husband, Emperor Sovieshu of the Eastern Empire, according to Disney's synopsis. Their relationship fractures when Sovieshu falls in love with a runaway slave. Navier agrees to the emperor's request on one condition: that she be allowed to remarry Crown Prince Heinrey of the rival Western Kingdom. Disney's own summary card for the series describes the same setup more bluntly, saying Navier's husband "seeks divorce to wed his mistress."
 The cast is led by Shin Mina (Karma, Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha) as Empress Navier, Ju Jihoon (Light Shop, The Trauma Code: Heroes on Call) as Emperor Sovieshu, Lee Jongsuk (Big Mouth) as Crown Prince Heinrey and Lee Seyoung (The Red Sleeve, The Crowned Clown) as Rashta. Yeoh Geena and Hyun Choongyeol adapted the webtoon for the screen, and Cho Suwon (Still 17, Pinocchio) directed.
 The webtoon origin is not incidental. A property with nearly 3 billion views behind it arrives with an audience that already knows the story, which means an opening-window ranking measures, in part, demand that was assembled before the first episode was filmed.
 Disney's streaming business behind the claim
 Disney has spent the past year turning its streaming division into a profit centre, and viewing claims have become part of how it presents that business. In the quarter ended December 27, 2025, Disney's Entertainment SVOD revenue exceeded $5 billion, up 11%, while operating income rose 72% to $450 million . The materials for that quarter cited 122 million ad-supported streaming subscribers and said Disney+ and Hulu accounted for seven of the ten most-watched shows of 2025, on Nielsen data.
 The following quarter, SVOD operating income reached $582 million, up 88% from $310 million , and SVOD advertising revenue rose 12% to $821 million, with Disney attributing the gain to more impressions, partly offset by lower rates. That report carried no subscriber count. Without one, title-level claims like this one carry more of the burden of showing that audiences are growing.
 The SVOD business is also becoming more international, and more multilingual. On July 15, 2026, Disney+ began rolling out 17 new audio languages, bringing the total to 58 , with subtitles and captions in as many as 42 languages, six new interface languages and a right-to-left layout for Arabic and Hebrew. Disney's newsroom lists that language announcement as a related article beneath The Remarried Empress release. PPC Land's coverage at the time noted that Disney cited local originals including Perfect Crown, Dear Killer Nannies, Battle of Fates and The Boss as examples of international performance. Language reach is what allows a Korean-language series to rank in Mexico, Chile and Germany at the same time.
 On the advertising side, Disney moved its EMEA campaigns to its global Disney Ad Server in an announcement dated June 30, 2026. The Disney+ ad tier runs in 15 European markets, and Disney said its EMEA advertiser and partner base had grown by more than 25% since the start of 2025. Disney+ is integrated with more than ten demand-side platforms, including Amazon DSP, The Trade Desk and Google's Display & Video 360. In Germany, Disney+ and AGF said on November 4, 2026 that they would examine integrating the service into the country's official TV ratings , a review with no timetable. Until that kind of measurement exists, Disney's own counts remain the main source of audience figures for its streaming titles in that market.
 The structure of the services is shifting too. EMARKETER forecast in September 2026 that ten major US TV players would become six by 2027 , with Disney folding Hulu into Disney+. The phrase "Disney+ and Hulu globally" in the announcement reflects that integration: the record is reported as a single combined figure across both brands, with no split between them. In the United States, Hulu on Disney+ launched fully for bundle subscribers in March 2024 , integrating Hulu content into Disney+ search and recommendations.
 Korean content as a competitive asset
 Disney is not the first streamer to lean on Korean production for global reach, and Netflix has made the larger public commitment. Netflix committed $2.5 billion to South Korean content over four years in April 2023. According to Ampere, 52% of Netflix original TV seasons released in 2025 were in languages other than English, up from 49% in 2024, and Korean titles rose from 12% to 20% of those non-English releases. When Netflix published its first viewing report in December 2023 , covering more than 18,000 titles for January to June 2023, non-English stories accounted for 30% of all viewing.
 Audiences in South Korea itself report a high tolerance for advertising. A Magnite survey of 905 South Korean adults, published on October 26, 2026, found that 67% of streamers use ad-supported services and accept seven minutes of ads per hour , with respondents using an average of five services. The survey also found that 69% of CTV and IPTV streamers often or always watch with others. The figures are self-reported, and Magnite sells advertising inventory, so the results come from a company with an interest in the answer.
 Self-reported superlatives are an industry habit
 Disney's claim fits a pattern across the large streamers, where rankings are published without the numbers that would let anyone check them. Prime Video called Maxton Hall its most-watched International Original ever in September 2026 without disclosing viewership figures. Amazon's Rings of Power viewer claim rose by 15 million to 185 million ahead of the third season , with its season rankings measured over 91-day windows of the company's choosing. Disney's own Toy Story 5 announcement used a five-day window. The Remarried Empress used three.
 Each company chooses its window, its definition of a view and its comparison set. The results are not comparable with one another, and often not even with the same company's previous claims. A three-day ranking and a five-day ranking from the same streamer measure different things. Is a three-day local original record a large number? Without the count, there is no way to know.
 Why this matters for marketers
 For media buyers, the practical issue is that the most specific audience signal Disney published about this series is a rank. Advertisers planning against Disney's streaming inventory in the weeks to the November 25 finale have a ranking among local originals, a ranking among Korean premieres, a trailer view count and a webtoon view count. They do not have a reach number, an ad-tier share, a demographic profile or a market-level split.
 That gap matters more as Disney sells streaming inventory through programmatic channels. A ranking does not tell buyers using demand-side platforms how much of a title's audience sits on ad-supported plans, or in which markets.
 The announcement does confirm three things that are useful on their own terms. Disney is putting promotional weight behind non-English productions in a period when its streaming business is reporting rising profit. The series runs weekly until the day before Thanksgiving, keeping it on the service through the start of the holiday retail season. And the global framing, across more than 50 markets, puts Disney's Korean output in the same international contest where Netflix has spent heavily on Korean production.
 Whether the record holds up beyond the opening window is a separate question. With six more episodes still to come, a later Disney update could show whether audiences stayed past the first four.

 Summary
 Who: The Walt Disney Company, for its Disney+ and Hulu streaming services, and the Korean series The Remarried Empress, starring Shin Mina, Ju Jihoon, Lee Jongsuk and Lee Seyoung, directed by Cho Suwon and adapted from a NAVER WEBTOON.
 What: Disney said the series became the most viewed local original premiere of all time on Disney+ and Hulu globally, based on three days of views, and ranks as the number one Korean title premiere in over 50 markets. Disney published no view count, no definition of a view or of a local original, no previous record holder and no ad-tier breakdown.
 When: The series launched on November 3, 2026, a day earlier than its scheduled November 4 premiere. Disney published the ranking on November 6, 2026. Two episodes follow each Wednesday from November 11 to the finale on November 25.
 Where: Disney+ and Hulu worldwide, with the Korean premiere ranking applying in more than 50 markets including the US, the UK, France, Spain, Germany, Mexico, Chile, Australia and New Zealand, and Canada.
 Why: Disney's streaming business is reporting rising profit and advertising revenue, its latest reported quarter carried no subscriber count, and it has expanded Disney+ to 58 audio languages to carry local productions across borders. A record for a Korean original supports that strategy, but without an absolute count, advertisers and analysts cannot compare it with other titles or services.
